purpose: Named product-level examples in which a regulator-authored or regulator-hosted source documents material use of a NAM or scientifically justified omission of legacy studies in regulatory decision-making. This dataset is broader than animal-study displacement: every record states what evidence was displaced, omitted, supplemented or unavailable.

cases.regulator: FDA CDER/OND; corroborated by EMA, TGA and Health Canada
cases.jurisdiction: United States / European Union / Australia / Canada
cases.nam: Human tissue and cell-based in vitro assays assessing target/species specificity, tissue cross-reactivity, organ-specific toxicity potential, cytokines and cytolytic proteins
cases.regulatory_impact: Supported clinical development and approval in the absence of a pharmacologically relevant animal model.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: A pharmacologically relevant animal toxicology species was unavailable; carcinogenicity, genotoxicity and reproductive/developmental studies were not conducted.
cases.note: Do not describe as a one-for-one waiver of a named mandatory test. The stronger claim is that multiple regulators independently recognized species irrelevance and accepted a human-specific evidence strategy.

cases.nam: In vitro characterization and safety studies, literature-based on-target/off-tumour assessment, human-membrane-protein/off-target assays and clinical evidence
cases.regulatory_impact: EMA accepted a nonclinical safety package without formal GLP toxicology and without repeat-dose toxicity because no relevant animal model was available; PMDA independently confirmed lack of a pharmacologically relevant rodent or NHP species.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Formal GLP toxicology and repeat-dose toxicity were not performed as the conventional safety strategy.
cases.note: Not an animal-free development program; limited in vivo pharmacology work remained.

cases.nam: Product-specific in vitro expansion/transformation studies, genomic insertion-site analysis and tailored nonclinical evidence
cases.regulatory_impact: CHMP accepted the absence of standard single- and repeat-dose toxicity studies because the patient-specific product was not appropriate for immunocompetent animals; conventional rodent genotoxicity/carcinogenicity models were also considered inappropriate.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Standard single-dose toxicity, repeat-dose toxicity and conventional rodent genotoxicity/carcinogenicity testing were not used as the relevant safety strategy.
cases.note: Selected immunocompromised-mouse studies were still used for narrower persistence/tumour-growth questions.

cases.nam: Product-specific characterization and clinical/post-market risk management; selected surrogate pharmacology rather than a conventional toxicology battery
cases.regulatory_impact: Health Canada authorized Yescarta while explicitly recording that no in vitro, ex vivo or in vivo model could accurately examine the toxicological characteristics of the individualized human product and that traditional toxicology, carcinogenicity and genotoxicity studies were not performed.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Traditional toxicology, carcinogenicity and genotoxicity studies were not performed; fertility, reproduction and development were not studied.
cases.note: Surrogate animal pharmacology existed for selected questions; this is not an animal-free program.

cases.nam: Human-tissue cross-reactivity, lentiviral integration-site mapping and in vitro IL-2-independent expansion/transformation testing
cases.regulatory_impact: Health Canada accepted a tailored nonclinical package centered on human tissue and product-specific in vitro/genomic assays; genotoxicity and carcinogenicity studies were not conducted and fertility studies were omitted given the product nature.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Conventional genotoxicity, carcinogenicity and fertility studies were not conducted; EMA separately records broader traditional-toxicity omission because of lack of species cross-reactivity.
cases.note: The confirmed Health Canada claim is narrower than the full EMA indexed toxicology statement; preserve that distinction.

cases.nam: Product-specific functional, insertional-risk and tumorigenic-risk evidence integrated with selected xenograft pharmacology
cases.regulatory_impact: Health Canada accepted the absence of traditional toxicity and fertility studies for the autologous CAR-T product; repeat-dose studies were not conducted because the product is administered as a single infusion.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Traditional toxicity and fertility studies and repeat-dose toxicology were not conducted.
cases.note: Mouse xenograft pharmacology remained informative for tumour-control questions; the claim is omission of conventional safety studies, not absence of all animal work.

cases.nam: In vitro CAR-T functional studies, vector-integration analysis and selected surrogate mouse pharmacology
cases.regulatory_impact: Health Canada states that no representative in vitro, ex vivo or in vivo model could accurately address toxicological characteristics of the engineered human T-cell product; traditional toxicology studies were therefore not performed.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Traditional toxicology, carcinogenicity, genotoxicity and reproductive/developmental studies were not conducted.
cases.note: A murine anti-CD19 surrogate model was used for selected pharmacology, so this is tailored use rather than an animal-free program.

cases.nam: In silico and in vitro healthy-human-tissue characterization, peptide cross-reactivity screens, primary human cells, iPSC-derived cells and organotypic models, plus vector-integration analysis
cases.regulatory_impact: FDA accepted a nonclinical package in which human-relevant in vitro systems addressed off-tumour/cross-reactivity questions; traditional genotoxicity/carcinogenicity assessments were not conducted and animal reproductive/developmental studies were omitted as acceptable based on product characteristics and safety profile.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Traditional in vitro/in vivo genotoxicity and carcinogenicity assessments and animal reproductive/developmental toxicity studies were not conducted.
cases.note: Murine xenografts were still used for antitumour pharmacology. The important extension is beyond CAR-T into an affinity-enhanced TCR-T therapy.

cases.regulator: Health Canada, based on TGA-led nonclinical work-share
cases.nam: Species-specific biologic risk assessment; EMA materials additionally describe human-tissue cross-reactivity for target-organ identification
cases.regulatory_impact: Health Canada records that the nonclinical evaluation was limited by species specificity and that embryofetal development effects were not investigated because appropriate animal models were absent.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Embryofetal development testing was omitted for lack of an appropriate animal model; genotoxicity, carcinogenicity and several reproductive studies were also not submitted under applicable ICH frameworks.
cases.note: A GLP main toxicity study existed, so Sarclisa must not be described as wholesale animal-toxicology omission.

cases.nam: Cell-based complement assays and validated ex vivo CH50 hemolysis assay
cases.regulatory_impact: Mechanistic nonclinical NAM data, together with correlating clinical data, served as confirmatory evidence supporting substantial evidence of efficacy and approval.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: No pharmacologically relevant species existed for key complement pharmacology; the totality nevertheless included animal and human data.
cases.note: Count as NAM reliance, not pure animal-study displacement.

cases.nam: In vitro CFTR chloride-transport assays using mutant CFTR systems including human bronchial epithelial cells
cases.regulatory_impact: Supported expansion to specific CFTR variants without additional clinical trials for each variant.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Additional variant-specific clinical trials, not an animal study.
cases.note: NAM adoption precedent, but not animal displacement.

cases.nam: In vitro alpha-galactosidase A activity assay in cells expressing specific GLA variants
cases.regulatory_impact: FDA accepted assay-response thresholds to identify amenable variants and expand the indicated genetic population without separate pre-approval clinical trials for every variant, with post-approval clinical verification.
cases.legacy_evidence_displaced_or_unavailable: Additional variant-specific clinical trials, not an animal study.
cases.note: NAM adoption precedent but not animal displacement; useful example of staged regulatory reliance.
